spells.name: Cazic Touch
spells.description: Otherwise known as "Death Touch", this is an instant cast skill a number of high level Classic-era raid mobs have. As the nickname suggests, it is an unresistable instant kill with a 30 second cooldown that has to be managed by the raid. Pullers often act as sacrificial lambs for the ability, aggroing the mob and kiting them around until they get deathtouched so their tanks don't have to. Its namesake, Cazic Thule (God) was the first NPC with this ability. Several others in Plane of Sky were also given it, such as Keeper of Souls, Spiroc Lord, Sister of the Spire, and the sphinxes on island 7. No NPCs in Velious were given this ability, as the 32k HP hard-cap was lifted, providing sufficient challenge for players without it. Mobs that have this ability won't always open with it. More so, they have a high chance of using it each second while aggroed - I've seen mobs in Sky wait 20 seconds before DTing, but the average wait is usually 3-10 seconds.

spells.name: Focus of Spirit
spells.description:
Focuses your target's spiritual energy, granting increased hit points, strength, and dexterity for 1 hour(s) 40.0 mins.
This spell has an unusual stacking mechanic. If a character has Focus, it will block the addition of Maniacal Strength, Mortal Deftness, and Voice of the Berserker spells. ''However'' if the character already has those buffs prior, the addition of Focus on top of those will not overwrite them, rather it will stack and both will apply to the character's statistics. Therefore, if a melee character would like all three buffs, they should click off any pre-existing Focus, then ask the Shaman for them.
Focus of Spirit will always overwrite other Talisman spells however. It also seems to overwrite lower level spells such as Dexterity.

Does not stack with Shield of the Magi and other INT caster HP buffs. Does not stack with Bedlam and other enchanter mat-free runes in that line. Does stack with Resurrection Effects.

spells.name: Knockback
spells.description:
Hurls your target back through the air in a shallow, horizontal arc.

When cast on the player by NPCs such as tentacle terrors, the player flies (often quite a considerable distance) in the opposite direction from where they are facing. The position of the NPC and player do not matter. Levitate and related effects will mitigate knockback's movement.

When a player applies this effect to an NPC, the distance the NPC is knocked back is much less. The direction of the knockback is on the same vector as where the casting player is facing, regardless of the NPC's position or facing direction. Hate generated from this effect is between 25 and 100.

When a player applies the effect to themselves, they are always knocked back due south.

spells.name: Ro's Fiery Sundering
spells.description: Surrounds your target in dancing flames, lowering their fire resistance and armor class. This spell generates a large amount of hate. Note: Didn't have a Fire (-200) resist modifier until 2002 because the "Resistadj" value wasn't created until then,[https://lucy.allakhazam.com/spellhistory.html?id=1437&source=Live] although the same patch that added Fire (-200) to Ro's Fiery Sundering also removed the pre-existing line "Slot 1: Lure(6)", implying that the spell was already abnormally hard to resist before the update that introduced the "Resistadj" value to the spell system. Prior to 2002, spells didn't have an entry for "Resistadj", with more difficult spells simply being given a "Lure" designation with some numerical value indicating how lure-y they were. In Lucy, the line reporting that the Resistadj value was changed from 0 to -200 was simply an indicator that the value was first created in the system. For context, Lure of Flame was marked as "Slot 1: Lure(5)" before the same patch on 2002-9-04 that updated Ro's Fiery Sundering to Fire (-200). The same patch in 2002 that removed "Slot 1: Lure(5)" from Lure of Flame also changed the Resistadj value from 0 to -300 for Lure of Flame, as well. Clearly, Lure of Flame did not actually have a Resistadj value of 0 before this patch; rather, the Resistadj value did not exist at all, and instead, stating that it was changed from 0 to -300 was Lucy's way of indicating that this new, unified Resistadj system had been added to replace the prior "Lure" designation that certain spells had. This was one part of several reworkings of the spell resist system that the old EQ devs had implemented over time. [https://lucy.allakhazam.com/spellhistory.html?id=1638&source=Live]

spells.name: Tishan's Relocation
spells.description: Opens an arcane portal that teleports your entire group to the Skyfire Mountains. This spell no longer has a Kunark dungeon requirement; it can currently be cast from anywhere in the world. '''Warning: The port in location for this spell is very dangerous.''' If you port in while visible, you will most likely die when alone or porting another. There are swarms of dispelling mobs at the zone in area. However, while invis, this port in location is nearly 100% safe. No mobs see invis and the only threat is the possibility of it breaking early. You can enter the zone invisibly by getting a friendly person to invis prime you. To perform this, join a group, and have that person begin to invis you. Before their cast finishes, begin your cast of Tishan's Relocation. Once their invis hits you, disband or have them disband before you finish the cast. You will port over to skyfire while remaining invis, as finishing casts does not break invisibility. With a primed invis, the port in at skyfire is much safer, and a very useful tool to Wizards.

spells.name: Torrent of Poison
spells.description:
Creates a rain of poison, causing 1-3 waves of 540 damage to 1-4 creatures in a small radius around your target.
At 1620-2160 damage, the potential blowback from this spell is significant. '''Use with extreme caution''' as it seems to prioritize hitting yourself up to twice if you cast it too close to the selected creature.
This spell seems to either hit four creatures one time,
Two creatures twice,
one creature three times,
or if cast on three creatures it will hit all three and then the original target once more.
If cast on a single creature while you're close to it, there's a chance of yourself and the creature getting hit twice each, or the creature getting hit three times and yourself once.
Despite having no resistance modifier, this spell has a high resist rate on creatures that normally could be hit by every spell you throw their way.

spells.name: Unswerving Hammer
spells.description: Summons a magical hammer that attacks your target relentlessly until either the hammer or the target dies. If there are additional mobs on the hammer's hate list, the hammer will stay alive and attack those mobs. The summoning cleric cannot control this hammer at all; e.g., it will always taunt. Using "Go Away" is of unknown use. The hammer has approximately 10 hp and cannot receive damage shields. It has a max hit of 40-45 depending on level. It can be given most other buffs once summoned (this was removed in later eras). This spell does work in Plane of Sky and the hammer appears normally there. While the spell lists no range, the hammer will despawn very quickly if the target is not close enough to the hammer to begin an initial attack. The pet may be reclaimed with Reclaim Energy, which increases the utility of the hammer somewhat. This pet is situationally useful for long melee-heavy fights with no AE spells such as Ulump Pujluk or An enraged golem. This spell is called Unswerving Hammer of Faith once scribed.

spells.name: Voice of the Berserker
spells.description:
Fills you with a berserk fury, increasing your strength, dexterity, and armor class for 18.7 mins @L59 to 20.5 mins @L65.
Unlike Fury, Frenzy, and Rage, three earlier self only shaman spells, this one does NOT drain mana rapidly, making this an actual viable spell that might get cast now and then. It does however prevent casting spells for 30 seconds.
Prevents the three previous mentioned spells and Fleeting Fury from sticking.
If for some reason you don't have max wisdom at level 59 or 60, you can pair this with Mortal Deftness and Manicial Strength and Focus of Spirit for 194 134 bonus Dex and a whopping 219 bonus strength, and use your maxed out str/dex for blacksmithing and fletching respectively.
Edit: Voice of the Berserker overrides Mortal Deftness, and Speed of the Shissar overrides Voice of the Berserker. Primal Essence does not interfere with Voice of the Berserker. Casting this spell will cause your spell gems to grey out for 30 seconds but a simple click on any "GCD" item will unlock this and let you cast like normal immediately afterwards.
